findings.issue: ROOT CAUSE of the builder's unexplained host exits — reproduced and captured in the host log. MainLayout starts the session's background work from ShellServices.Changed (HandleShellChanged -> `_ = InvokeAsync(async () => await StartBackgroundWorkAsync())`). AccountSession raises that event in the MIDDLE of LockService.UnlockAsync, so the fire-and-forget task runs Shell.Clock.StartAsync (a clock check that writes) and Shell.Badges.RefreshAsync on the SAME WakeelDb instance UnlockAsync is still using for its audit write. WpfDispatcher.InvokeAsync(Func<Task>) does not await the inner task, so the two overlap. Unlocking after the idle lock killed the window: 'System.InvalidOperationException: A second operation was started on this context instance before a previous operation completed' at WakeelDb.SaveChangesAsync <- AuditService.LogAsync <- LockService.UnlockAsync:224 <- W06LockOverlay.UnlockAsync:91, logged as [FTL] Unhandled exception, process exited. The try/catch the builder added inside BackgroundPassDispatcher does not help: the victim is the FOREGROUND operation, which is unguarded.
findings.fix: Serialize every DbContext use of the open session. (1) Add `private readonly SemaphoreSlim _gate = new(1,1);` to src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Shell/ShellServices.cs and expose `Task RunExclusiveAsync(Func<Task>)` / `Task<T> RunExclusiveAsync<T>(Func<Task<T>>)` that takes the gate. (2) Route MainLayout's StartBackgroundWorkAsync, RefreshBadgesAsync and the body of the BackgroundPassDispatcher lambda through it. (3) Take the same gate around the DB work in src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/LockService.UnlockAsync and the sign-out path (both inside allowed paths). (4) Stop starting background work from inside the Changed handler: have HandleShellChanged set `_needsStart = true; StateHasChanged();` and do the start in OnAfterRenderAsync, so it can never overlap the session operation that raised the event.

findings.issue: The «تراجع» the B2 spec requires for W94 («حفظ فوري وToast مع «تراجع»», AGREEMENT item 32) is invisible in the running host. Lines 25-26 and 31 use the FUNCTIONAL form `.w-undo ::deep(.w-undo-action)`, which the Blazor scoped-CSS rewriter emits verbatim as `.w-undo[b-3f5l9g1azc] (.w-undo-action)` — an invalid selector the browser drops (confirmed in src/Wakeel.UI/obj/Debug/net10.0/scopedcss/bundle/Wakeel.UI.styles.css lines 28-34). The button therefore keeps WButton's default text colour: measured over CDP after a real quick-capture save, «تراجع» is rgb(45,111,102) on the strip's rgb(49,115,93) fill — contrast approx 1.03:1, not visible at all; the ✕ is rgb(102,115,123) on the same green, approx 2.2:1.
findings.fix: Use the space form Blazor supports: `.w-undo ::deep .w-undo-action, .w-undo ::deep .w-undo-close { color: var(--w-on-fill); flex: none; }` and `.w-undo ::deep .w-undo-action { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: underline; }`. Verify the generated bundle contains `.w-undo[b-...] .w-undo-action`, not `[b-...] (...)`, and re-check the rendered colour in the host.

findings.issue: The dangerous-action consequence strip is illegible in the DARK theme. Lines 74-81: `.w-dialog-notice { background: var(--w-text); color: var(--w-white); }`. In dark theme --w-text resolves to rgb(230,236,239), so the strip is white-on-white — measured over CDP on /w92: bg rgb(230,236,239), colour rgb(255,255,255) for both «إجراء نهائي لا يمكن التراجع عنه» (danger dialog) and «وارد: 12/09/2026 · 05:11» (record-changed dialog). Light theme renders correctly as the dark strip the export draws, which is why it was missed. This hides the one sentence the person MUST read before an irreversible action, in every future Danger dialog in the product, not just the W92 sheet.
findings.fix: Make the strip invert with the theme instead of hard-coding white text: `.w-dialog-notice { background: var(--w-text); color: var(--w-bg); }` (or var(--w-surface)). Add a check in DailyShellComponentTests that the notice's colour token is not the same token family as its background in both themes.

findings.issue: Design-consistency rule (owner, 2026-09-16): a toast-with-action is a design-system surface, and one is hand-rolled here inside Wakeel.UI — its own `<div class="w-undo">` chrome plus page CSS — instead of living in src/Wakeel.Design/Components beside WToast/WToastHost. It has no Gallery entry and no bUnit test, which is exactly the process the rule requires («component + css + gallery entry + bUnit test, then use it»). It is also why the contrast bug above was never caught: nothing in the gallery or the suite ever renders it. The builder correctly moved W10's panel and rows into Wakeel.Design; this one was left behind.
findings.fix: Move it to src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WUndoToast.razor + WUndoToast.razor.css (with the corrected ::deep rules), add a Gallery.razor entry in the daily-shell section, add a bUnit test in tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/Components/DailyShellComponentTests.cs asserting the text, the «تراجع» label/tooltip and its OnUndo, and have MainLayout render the design component.

findings.issue: Same invalid `::deep(...)` syntax on line 27 (`.w91-cell ::deep(.w-state-card) { flex: 1; ... }`), so the rule is dropped and the cards never stretch to their grid cells. Measured in the host: the thirteen .w91-cell boxes are all exactly 201x221, but the WStateCards inside them are 122px («جارٍ التحميل»), 173px («تم الحفظ بنجاح»), 177px («فشلت العملية») and 194px for the rest — three cards are visibly narrower than their neighbours and sit off the column edge. The W91 export shows a uniform 5-up grid with every card filling its cell. Visible in both themes.
findings.fix: `.w91-cell ::deep .w-state-card { flex: 1; ... }` (space, not parentheses). Re-measure in the host: all thirteen inner cards must report the same width as their cells.

findings.issue: W10 does not drop out of the bell. Line 14 pins the panel with a hard-coded `inset-inline-start: 256px`, i.e. to the inline-start edge of the content area, not to the bell. Measured in the host at 1366x768: panel left=721 width=380 (start/right edge 1101) while the bell's right edge is ~895 — the panel's start edge is 206px past the bell. The W10 export clearly hangs the panel from the bell. It also hard-codes a sidebar width inside a component that knows nothing about the shell's sidebar.
findings.fix: Anchor the panel to the bell: render WNotificationPanel inside a `position: relative` wrapper in WTopBar's action cluster and position it with `inset-inline-start: 0; inset-block-start: 100%` on that wrapper, or pass the anchor offset in as a parameter. At the bell's position the 380px panel still fits entirely inside the content area, so the sidebar overlap the builder fixed does not come back.

findings.issue: The footer link «عرض كل الإشعارات» is wired to `OnClick="OpenSettingsAsync"` (line ~68), the same handler as the gear, so it navigates to W10NotificationPanel.SettingsRoute = "/w86" — the settings screen. The label promises the full notification list. Today it lands on «الصفحة غير موجودة»; once W86 exists it will silently land on settings, which is worse than the missing-page answer.
findings.fix: Give the footer its own route constant and handler (the notifications list screen the export implies). Until that page exists, point it at a dedicated placeholder route or remove the footer link — do not reuse the settings route. Extend the W10 navigation test in ShellSurfaceTests to assert the gear and the footer go to DIFFERENT routes.

findings.issue: The undo strip never expires. HandleCapturedAsync sets _undoText/_undoToken and nothing clears them except the person pressing ✕ or «تراجع» (ClearUndo/UndoAsync). Observed in the host: after one quick capture the strip stayed on screen indefinitely, covering the start of the side column. The spec asks for a Toast; a toast fades. Worse, `CanUndo="@(_undoToken is not null)"` stays true forever, so the button keeps offering an undo whose token has long expired and the person gets «انتهت مهلة التراجع» instead.
findings.fix: On capture, start a timer from the injected TimeProvider for the undo window QuickCaptureService honours: flip CanUndo to false when the token expires and clear _undoText at/after that moment, always through InvokeAsync. Add a bUnit test that advances a FakeTimeProvider and asserts the strip disappears and «تراجع» is gone once the window has passed.

findings.issue: Side-by-side with design/exports/preview/light/W/W94: the export's task form has FOUR fields — «العنوان *», «تاريخ الاستحقاق *» + «الأولوية», «الربط بمراسلة (اختياري)», «ملاحظة (اختياري)» (a textarea). The host renders three and has no note field at all for a task, although the note/expense/appointment branches all have one. The export also marks «تاريخ الاستحقاق» required (red *) where the host leaves it optional with a +7-day default. (The «المكلّف» vs «الربط بمراسلة» swap is a reasonable deferral until B3; the missing note is not.)
findings.fix: Add the optional «ملاحظة (اختياري)» textarea (Ar.QuickCapture.ExtraNoteLabel/ExtraNotePlaceholder already exist) to the Task branch, bound to a field distinct from _title, and pass it to CaptureTaskAsync (or wherever the service takes a note). Extend the W94 task test in ShellSurfaceTests to assert the saved task carries it.

findings.issue: The spec for W92 is «صفحة مرجعية للحوارات ... مع التلميحات». The DialogEntry record carries Trigger, ConfirmTooltip and CancelTooltip (Ar.StandardDialogs.DangerConfirmTooltip, ConflictTakeIncomingTooltip, RecordChangedRefreshTooltip, …) but none of those three members is ever read in the markup — WDialog falls back to Tooltip=Label for both buttons. The sheet shows generic tooltips and three Ar strings are dead.
findings.fix: Either add ConfirmTooltip/CancelTooltip parameters to WDialog (defaulting to the labels, so no existing caller changes) and pass the sheet's values, or delete the unused record members and the orphaned Ar constants. Assert the rendered title attribute in HealthAndReferenceScreenTests.

findings.issue: Beside design/exports/preview/dark/W/W09: the export's header carries «تصدير القائمة» beside «معالجة التالي» (host has «تحديث» instead); a second filter row with «تصفية», an «الأكثر تأخرًا أولاً» sort and the note «أطول تأخر: 23 يومًا · 5 سجلات تجاوزت أسبوعين»; and a pager (‹ 1 2 ›) under the table. None exists in the host, and the tabs are WTabs underline where the export draws filled pills. None is required by the B2 spec text, so these are defensible — but the missing pager matters for another reason: the screen calls GetAllAsync and renders EVERY row, so a real office's overdue list is unbounded. The 7-column table also produces a horizontal scrollbar at 1366x768 the export does not have.
findings.fix: Keep the underline tabs (one tab component in the product is the right call). Record the export/filter/sort/pager as deferred. For the unbounded list, cap the rendered rows or add the pager. For the overflow, let «الإجراء التالي» wrap and drop the fixed min-widths in W09Overdue.razor.css so seven columns fit at 1366.

findings.issue: Beside the W08 export (light and dark): the «يحتاج إجراءً اليوم» section header keeps title and the four tabs on one row but pushes the local search onto a second row, where the export keeps title + tabs + search on one line; the same happens to «عرض كل المصروفات» on the phone-expenses card. The expenses table shows a horizontal scrollbar the export does not. The KPI icons are bare outlines where the export draws each in a tinted rounded square, and the sync/backup cards lack the export's third detail row («الوجهة … الحجم … التالية») and its «مزامنة الآن» action.
findings.fix: Let .w08-filters share one line: nowrap with `min-width: 0` on the children and `flex: 1 1 160px` on the search. Give the expenses table the same column relaxation as W09. Move the KPI icon square into WKpiCard's own CSS (`.w-kpi-icon { background: var(--w-surface2); border-radius: var(--w-radius); padding: 6px; }`) so every screen inherits it.

findings.issue: Beside the export: each state's icon is coloured by severity there (red for «القاعدة غير متاحة», amber for «تعذّر فتح الملف»/«فشلت العملية», teal for «تم الحفظ بنجاح», grey for neutral) while every host card draws the same muted grey circle, so the sheet no longer teaches which state carries which tone. The export also has a «تحديث» header action the host lacks.
findings.fix: Add an optional Variant (WSemanticVariant) parameter to WStateCard that tints .w-state-icon, defaulting to Neutral so no existing caller changes, and set it per entry in the W91 table. Cover it in the design-component tests.

findings.issue: Arabic agreement in the due cell: the host renders «متأخر يومان (15/09/2026)» because DueText composes Ar.Overdue.LateByDays(CoreAr.DaysPhrase(item.DaysLate)) and DaysPhrase returns the nominative dual «يومان»; the W08 and W09 exports both read «متأخر يومين». (The same phrase in W09's «التأخر بالأيام» column, standing alone, is correct.)
findings.fix: The phrase needs the oblique dual after «متأخر». Either add a CoreAr overload returning «يومين» for the adverbial position, or change Ar.Overdue.LateByDays to take the count and build «متأخر يومين» itself. CoreAr is Wakeel.Core — outside this package's allowed edits — so raise it with the services package rather than editing it here.

findings.issue: Observed in the host after the idle lock fired: the sidebar and bell fall back to the FIXED SAMPLE badge numbers (العمل اليومي 18, مركز الانتباه 5, المراسلات 12, المتابعة والمهام 3, المالية والتقارير 2, bell 3) behind the lock overlay, because StartBackgroundWorkAsync nulls _liveBadges when the session closes and Badges/BellCount then return SampleBadges/SampleNotificationCount. A locked shell showing invented counts of real office work is misleading, and the numbers are legible around the overlay.
findings.fix: Distinguish 'no session yet' (first paint before sign-in, where the fixed sample dataset is right) from 'session closed by a lock/sign-out'. Keep a _hadSession flag: once a session has been open, fall back to an empty badge dictionary and a zero bell instead of the sample numbers.

findings.issue: W08's «يحتاج إجراءً اليوم» rows are clickable `<tr ... @onclick="OpenRecord">` with no role, tabindex or key handler, so a row cannot be reached from the keyboard; W09's visually identical rows are not clickable at all and offer only the «معالجة» button. The two screens teach different interactions for the same row.
findings.fix: Pick one: make the row a keyboard-reachable target in both screens (tabindex="0", role="button", @onkeydown for Enter/Space — better, add an OnRowClick parameter to WTable so every table in the product behaves the same), or drop the row click on W08 and turn its chevron cell into a real WButton like W09's.

missing_spec_items: W08 monthly-report banner: the readiness percentage and missing-items list from ReadinessService. The banner shows the financial-cycle sentence with 0% and «لم تُحسب بنود الجاهزية بعد» where the export reads «الجاهزية 80 بالمئة — 8 من 10 بنود مكتملة». The B2 spec explicitly permits this («بيانات حقيقية من ReadinessService إن وُجدت أو 0 مؤقتًا») and ReadinessService is B5's — accepted, listed so B5 picks it up.

W92 «مع التلميحات»: the per-dialog confirm/cancel tooltips are written in Ar.StandardDialogs and carried in the page's DialogEntry record but never rendered (WDialog has no tooltip parameters); the buttons show their own labels instead.
W94 task form: the export's optional «ملاحظة (اختياري)» field is absent, and «تاريخ الاستحقاق» is not marked required as the export marks it.
W94 «الربط بمراسلة (اختياري)» replaced by «المكلّف (اختياري)» — correctly deferred until B3 builds correspondence.

W09: «تصدير القائمة», the «تصفية» / «الأكثر تأخرًا أولاً» controls and the pager the export draws are absent. None is in the B2 spec text, so this is a deviation from the export rather than a missing spec item — but the missing pager also means the screen renders every overdue record with no cap.

Cross-screen links that land on «الصفحة غير موجودة» until later packages exist: /w70 (monthly report), /w39 (calendar), /w66 (all expenses), /w86 (settings) and every route in RecordRoutes.cs. Correctly documented by the builder; only W10's footer misuse of /w86 (medium finding) is a defect.
notes:
BUILD AND TESTS — both green, exactly as reported. `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) (TreatWarningsAsErrors is on, so warnings-as-errors is clean). `dotnet build tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests --no-dependencies` -> 0/0. `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests --no-build` -> Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 308, Skipped: 0, Total: 308, 25s. No NuGet package added; nothing outside the package's allowed paths touched; I modified nothing.

HOST RUN I DID MYSELF. Seeded a fresh temporary data folder with HostDataFolderSeed (WAKEEL_HOST_ROOT), launched src/Wakeel.Desktop/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Wakeel.Desktop.exe --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<temp> --start-url=/w08, confirmed http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/version, signed in over CDP with the seeded password, and screenshotted W08 (dark, top and scrolled), W10 (dark), W09 (dark), W12 (dark), W91 (dark+light), W92 (dark+light), W94 (light) and the undo strip (light) at 1366x768, each opened once beside design/exports/preview/{dark,light}/W/*.jpg. The process is killed; tasklist confirms no Wakeel host is running. W11 is not reachable without changing this machine's clock (a prohibited action); its six bUnit tests are honest — they drive ClockGuard.CheckAsync with a five-year-old instant and assert the title, the numbering notice, both tooltips, that «تجاهل مؤقتًا» hides the banner while NumberingBlocked stays true, and that «تصحيح الساعة» calls ISystemSettingsLauncher exactly once.

LIVE EVIDENCE THAT THE SHELL WIRING WORKS. The bell badge went 3 -> 4 during the session and the panel showed a new «حان وقت النسخ الاحتياطي · قبل دقيقة» row that was not seeded — the ReminderScheduler minute tick really runs through the renderer and BadgeService really re-counts. «الكل 5 / غير المقروء 4» matched the store. On the idle lock the live badges dropped and the panel closed, so the stop path fires. W08's «تأكيد»/«رفض» rows, the KPI colours, the four tabs, the local searches, W12's eleven cards with their filter counts, W91's thirteen states and W92's five surfaces all rendered against real data, and the PageHeaderState ownership fix is visibly working (W91/W92 keep their title rows).

THE HOST STABILITY ISSUE IS ROOT-CAUSED — see the first high finding. It is not in ReminderScheduler/BadgeService/HealthService or the Windows probes as the builder guessed; it is the shell wiring in MainLayout racing LockService.UnlockAsync on the one shared WakeelDb. Full stack in <data-folder>/logs/wakeel-20260917.log ([ERR] Unhandled UI-thread exception 02:40:12.839, [FTL] 02:40:12.844). It reproduced on my first unlock, about two minutes into the session, and the window died. The log otherwise holds only «Wakeel desktop host starting up» — no secret, no password, no mention of a server, port or database.

THE TWO INVISIBLE-CONTROL BUGS SHARE ONE CAUSE. `::deep(.x)` is not the syntax Blazor's scoped-CSS rewriter understands; it emits `[b-hash] (.x)`, which every browser discards. It appears three times in this package's CSS (UndoToast.razor.css x3, W91StandardStates.razor.css x1) and once pre-existing in src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WToastHost.razor.css:12 (`.w-toast-host ::deep(.w-toast)`), outside this package's diff but worth fixing in the same pass. bUnit cannot see this class of defect — only the host can — which is why 308 green tests coexist with an invisible «تراجع». After fixing, verify no `] (` sequence remains in src/Wakeel.UI/obj/Debug/net10.0/scopedcss/bundle/Wakeel.UI.styles.css.

WHAT I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN. No hand-rolled controls in any of the eight screens: grep for <button/<input/<select/<table/<ul/<textarea/role="tab"/role="dialog" across all eight page files returns nothing — the design-consistency pass is real (W10's panel and rows, W94's segmented strip, W92's inline dialogs are genuine Wakeel.Design components with CSS, Gallery entries and bUnit coverage). UndoToast is the one exception. The four extensions to existing components (WKpiCard OnClick/Tooltip/Variant/Class, WSegmented Icons/Stacked/Class, WDialog Notice/Inline/Class/MaxWidthPx, the close-cross title) are purely additive with safe defaults; the scope call was right — each removed a hand-rolled control. Security: no MarkupString anywhere in Wakeel.UI or Wakeel.Design except WIcon's compile-time SVG paths; Bidi.Wrap returns a plain escaped string, so no user data reaches markup unescaped; no technical term, error code, stack trace, server, port, internet or database mention in any state card, banner or toast (every failure path lands on Ar.Shell.ReadFailedTitle/Desc, detail stays in the host log); the health report is written only through WindowsFileSaveService's SaveFileDialog and contains only IHealthService.ExportText's Arabic sentences; ms-settings:dateandtime is a compile-time constant with UseShellExecute, no data path into the command line; no password, key or seed reaches logs or UI state. Background passes go through ComponentBase.InvokeAsync as BackgroundPassDispatcher (correct shape), and the guard/scheduler stop explicitly on the user-menu lock and sign-out and implicitly by scope disposal on the idle lock — the concurrency defect is about WHEN they start, not whether they stop. RTL/bidi: bdi/Bidi.Wrap on every Latin or numeric token I saw (amounts, dates, relative times, KPI numbers, device names); nothing reordered wrongly in any screenshot. Every icon-only button carries a tooltip (the bell and calendar use the product's w-tooltip-wrap component rather than a title attribute; WDialog's close cross has both aria-label and title). Tests assert real behaviour, not tautologies: DB rows, NavigationManager URIs, unread counts after MarkRead, tab counts, tooltip attributes, a recording ISystemSettingsLauncher for W11, and the two W07 RecoveredNotSignedIn paths reached deterministically — both carry-over findings are genuinely closed. The PhoneExpenseReview foreign-key fix is correct: three saves in FK order inside one transaction, with a caller's existing transaction respected. Minor process note: HostDataFolderSeed is a [Fact] that returns immediately without WAKEEL_HOST_ROOT, so it passes trivially and inflates the count by one — consider [Fact(Skip=...)] driven by the variable, or move it out of the test class.

VERDICT. Build and tests pass and the package is substantially complete and well built — but four high findings (a reproducible host crash, two controls rendered invisible by the same CSS-syntax bug, one of them the spec-mandated «تراجع», and a hand-rolled component the owner's rule forbids) and five medium ones mean it cannot be accepted as it stands. Every fix is small and inside the package's allowed paths.
